$$\begin{aligned} \int_{-3}^{8} f(x)\,dx &= \int_{-3}^{2} f(x)\,dx+\int_{2}^{8} f(x)\,dx \\ A &= \int_{-3}^{2} f(x)\,dx+B \\ \int_{-3}^{2} f(x)\,dx &= A-B \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \displaystyle\int_{2}^{-3} f(x)\,dx=-(A-B)=B-A$

Now

$$\begin{aligned} \int_{2}^{-3}\left(f(x)+2x\right)dx &= \int_{2}^{-3} f(x)\,dx+\int_{2}^{-3} 2x\,dx \\ &= B-A+\left[x^2\right]_{2}^{-3} \\ &= B-A+9-4 \\ &= B-A+5 \end{aligned}$$

$4\sin(x+\pi)=-4\sin x$, so the equation is $\cot\left(\dfrac{3x}{2}\right)=-4\sin x$.

Reflecting $y=4\sin x$ in the $x$-axis gives $y=-4\sin x$, which meets $y=\cot\left(\dfrac{3x}{2}\right)$ on $0\le x\le 2\pi$ once between $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, at $x=\pi$, and once between $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$: 3 solutions.

$\therefore B$

$$\begin{aligned} &\ln 3^8+\ln 3^{10}+\ln 3^{12}+\ldots+\ln 3^{2n} \\ &= 8\ln 3+10\ln 3+12\ln 3+\ldots+2n\ln 3 \\ &= \ln 3\,(8+10+12+\ldots+2n) \end{aligned}$$

Arithmetic series: $a=8$, $d=2$, $n-3$ terms, $l=2n$; $S_n=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)$

$$\begin{aligned} &= \ln 3\left[\dfrac{n-3}{2}(8+2n)\right] \\ &= \ln 3\left[\dfrac{n-3}{2}\cdot 2(4+n)\right] \\ &= (n-3)(n+4)\ln 3 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore D$

$\angle COM=120^\circ$

By the cosine rule:

$$\begin{aligned} CM^2 &= OC^2+OM^2-2\,OC\times OM\cos\angle COM \\ CM^2 &= 80^2+60^2-2\times 80\times 60\cos 120^\circ \\ CM^2 &= 80^2+60^2-2\times 80\times 60\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \\ CM^2 &= 14800 \\ CM &= \sqrt{14800}\quad (CM>0) \\ CM &= \sqrt{400\times 37} \\ &= 20\sqrt{37}\text{ km} \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
By the sine rule,

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\sin\angle CMO}{OC} &= \dfrac{\sin\angle COM}{CM} \\ \dfrac{\sin\angle CMO}{80} &= \dfrac{\sin 120^\circ}{20\sqrt{37}} \\ \sin\angle CMO &= \dfrac{80\sin 120^\circ}{20\sqrt{37}} \\ \angle CMO &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{80\sin 120^\circ}{20\sqrt{37}}\right) \\ &= 34.71500\ldots^\circ \\ &\approx 35^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Since $\angle COM=120^\circ$, so $\angle CMO$ must be acute.

$\therefore$ the bearing of the car from the motor bike is approximately $N55^\circ W$ or $305^\circ T$.

Alternatively, use cosine rule to find $\angle CMO$.

Stationary points ($y'=0$):

$$\begin{aligned} y' &= \dfrac{(x-2)\cdot 2x-x^2\cdot 1}{(x-2)^2} \\ &= \dfrac{2x^2-4x-x^2}{(x-2)^2} \\ &= \dfrac{x^2-4x}{(x-2)^2} \\ &= \dfrac{x(x-4)}{(x-2)^2} \end{aligned}$$

$=0$ when $x=0$ or when $x=4$

$\therefore$ $y=0$ or $y=8$

$\therefore$ stationary points $(0,0)$ and $(4,8)$

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dP}{dt} &= \dfrac{d}{dt}4000\left(1+15e^{-0.5t}\right)^{-1} \\ &= 4000(-1)\left(1+15e^{-0.5t}\right)^{-2}(-0.5)15e^{-0.5t} \\ &= \dfrac{30000e^{-0.5t}}{\left(1+15e^{-0.5t}\right)^2} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} x^2+ax+y^2+by+c &= 0 \\ \left(x+\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2-\dfrac{a^2}{4}+\left(y+\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2-\dfrac{b^2}{4}+c &= 0 \\ \left(x+\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2+\left(y+\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2 &= \dfrac{a^2}{4}+\dfrac{b^2}{4}-c \end{aligned}$$

Shifted to the right by 1:

$$\left(x-1+\dfrac{a}{2}\right)^2+\left(y+\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2=\dfrac{a^2}{4}+\dfrac{b^2}{4}-c$$

New centre at $(3,4)$:

$1-\dfrac{a}{2}=3$, $-\dfrac{b}{2}=4$

$a=-4$, $b=-8$

Radius is 3:

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{a^2}{4}+\dfrac{b^2}{4}-c &= 3^2 \\ \dfrac{4^2}{4}+\dfrac{(-8)^2}{4}-c &= 9 \\ c &= 4+16-9 \\ &= 11 \end{aligned}$$

Alternatively, set the original centre $(2,4)$:

$$\begin{aligned} (x-2)^2+(y-4)^2 &= 9 \\ x^2-4x+4+y^2-8y+16-9 &= 0 \\ x^2-4x+y^2-8y+11 &= 0 \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ $a=-4$, $b=-8$, $c=11$.

Hourly fuel cost $\propto x^2$

$$\begin{aligned} &= kx^2 \\ 2000 &= k\times 40^2 \\ \dfrac{2000}{1600} &= k \\ k &= 1.25=1\tfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{5}{4} \end{aligned}$$

Total cost per hour = hourly fuel cost + other costs per hour

Hourly cost $=\dfrac{5}{4}x^2+4800$

Total cost, $C=\left(\dfrac{5}{4}x^2+4800\right)\times$ number of hours

Speed $=\dfrac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}}$, so Time $=\dfrac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}}=\dfrac{B}{x}$

$$\begin{aligned} C &= \left(\dfrac{5}{4}x^2+4800\right)\times\dfrac{B}{x} \\ C &= B\left(\dfrac{5}{4}x+\dfrac{4800}{x}\right) \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} C &= B\left(\dfrac{5}{4}x+\dfrac{4800}{x}\right) \\ \dfrac{dC}{dx} &= B\left(\dfrac{5}{4}-4800x^{-2}\right) \\ &= B\left(\dfrac{5}{4}-\dfrac{4800}{x^2}\right) \end{aligned}$$

Stationary points occur when $\dfrac{dC}{dx}=0$:

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{5}{4}-\dfrac{4800}{x^2} &= 0 \\ \dfrac{5}{4} &= \dfrac{4800}{x^2} \\ 5x^2 &= 4800\times 4 \\ x^2 &= \dfrac{4800\times 4}{5} \\ x^2 &= 3840 \\ x &= \pm 61.96773354 \end{aligned}$$

but $x>0$ since speed is positive, $\therefore x=61.97$

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{d^2C}{dx^2} &= B\left(0-(-2)4800x^{-3}\right) \\ &= B\times\dfrac{9600}{x^3} \end{aligned}$$

When $x=\sqrt{3840}=61.9677$, $\dfrac{d^2C}{dx^2}=B\times\dfrac{9600}{61.9677^3}>0$ since $B>0$ as $B$ is a distance

$\therefore$ minimum cost, i.e. most economical speed when $x=\sqrt{3840}\approx 61.97$ km/h
